drivingQuestion: Is the mishna's clause on a vessel borrowed before the Festival redundant?
outcomeNote: Necessary for the case of delivery only on the Festival.

segments.he: הַשּׁוֹאֵל כְּלִי מֵחֲבֵירוֹ מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב. פְּשִׁיטָא! לָא צְרִיכָא, שֶׁלֹּא מְסָרוֹ לוֹ אֶלָּא בְּיוֹם טוֹב. מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: לָאו בִּרְשׁוּתֵיהּ אוֹקְמֵיהּ, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.
segments.en: § The mishna states: In the case of «one who borrows a vessel from another on the eve of a Festival,» it is as the feet of the borrower. The Gemara asks: It is «obvious» that this is the case, as the place of rest of the vessel has already been established in the possession of the borrower. The Gemara answers: «No,» it is «necessary» to state this halakha in a case «where one did not deliver» the vessel «to him until the Festival» itself. «Lest you say:» Since the lender «did not establish it in» the borrower’s «possession» before the Festival began, it should remain as the feet of the lender, the mishna therefore «teaches us» that it is not so, but it is as the feet of the borrower.
